newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cuba fishing tournament aims to diversify tourism.
newsitem.headline: Cuba fishing tournament aims to diversify tourism.

text.p: Cuban tour operators were in Mexico on Tuesday to launch the upcoming 47th Ernest Hemingway International Billfish Fishing Tournament as part of a drive to diversify Cuba's increasingly vital tourist trade.
"The Tournament is an important link with its founder, a great man who loved Cuba," said Marina Menocal, director of marketing and public relations at the Hemingway Marina on the outskirts of Havana.
Menocal flew to Mexico to promote the tournament, which will be held on May 19-24 in Cuba.
Nobel literature laureate Hemingway lived in Cuba for 22 years and his love of fishing and battling the elements were reflected in his novel "The Old Man And The Sea."

Mexico, along with Spain, Canada and Italy, provide Cuba with its greatest supply of tourists. They have become a hard-currency lifeline for the Communist-ruled island since the demise of the Soviet Union.
"We wish to promote Cuba as more of a destination for family vacations," a Cuban official, who asked not to be identified, said.
Echoing his words, one tour operator in Mexico stressed that the Caribbean island was more than a paradise of sun, rum and casual sex.
"I am broad-minded and people are free to do what they like, but there is far more to Cuba than people believe," Emilio Lang, Sales and Marketing Manager of Mexico-based Taino Tours told Reuters.

Lang said he had no interest in promoting the "empty recreation" of "jineteria," the Cuban term for young women who offer sexual favours to foreign tourists in return for a few hours of luxury and some scarce, hard currency.
Lang said his company also offered activities ranging from scuba diving to mountaineering.
During the heyday of Soviet economic aid for Cuba, Havana hotel lobbies frequented by foreign visitors were virtually out of bounds to Cubans.
Taino charters one flight a week to Cuba from Tijuana, on the United States border, for the benefit of U.S. tourists who wish to avoid Washington's ban on such travel, Lang said.
